plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A showpiece of the Cape. Each bloom is a dinner-plate-sized crown of stiff, silky-tipped bracts that fan out like a pink artichoke. Nectar-seeking sunbirds and beetles crowd around it in the cool, misty winter air of the fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter into spring (June to October), so late August is well within the flowering period
plants.location: Western Cape fynbos, South Africa (such as the slopes around Cape Town)
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Its family is so ancient that it dates back to when the southern continents were joined in Gondwana.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sun-chasing stalks carry huge golden faces ringed with bright petals and centered on dark, seed-packed discs. In late summer whole fields glow yellow and hum with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom runs from mid-July to late August in temperate Europe and North America, with some fields lasting into September
plants.location: Temperate Northern Hemisphere farmland and gardens, including Europe and the United States
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower. It is hundreds of tiny florets packed in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: In the Australian late winter, this small tree is covered in fluffy, honey-scented golden pom-poms. They light up the bush and roadsides against grey-green foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (roughly August to October), so it is in flower around August 29
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. Australians celebrate National Wattle Day on September 1, just after this date.
